summary: Vikram: 'add this to the appropriate menu on gridatlas and pipeline news', and 'why are the drop down engines here NOT in the menus of gridatlas and pipelinenews'. Both of this page's navs -- the desktop sidebar and the RELEASES popover a phone opens -- now carry the GB electricity price and grid constraint study, the engine graph, the federation map and the spider printer, plus one toggle that lists every node the engine genome publishes, grouped by kind, each linking to ?graph=engine-graph&focus=<label>. The study is also linked beside the product's existing OPEN GB ELECTRICITY CONTEXT button, which is where a reader of this product already goes for price.
modification_note: index.html: five rows appended after MAP ATLAS in each of the two navs (the same markup twice, no ids, so the mobile popover and the desktop sidebar stay interchangeable), and one link after the GB electricity opener. app.mjs: one lazy cross-origin read of ventus-grid-engine/genome/engine-graph.json and a click handler; the node list is never written in source, so a node added to the genome appears here with no edit and no second naming scheme to drift. GitHub Pages was verified to answer that URL with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * against a real Origin header before this was written. The fetch happens only when the reader opens the list, its failure prints its own reason where the list would have been, and the promise is cleared so the next tap is a real retry -- a menu whose contents fail silently is worse than one that does not offer them. The ENGINE GRAPH link beside it is a plain anchor and works whether any of that runs or not. No MutationObserver and no DOM observation of any kind: the toggle writes into one container it owns, on a click. orientation.css gains the toggle, the group heading, the failure line and an explicit .engine-nodes[hidden] rule, because display:flex on the container would otherwise beat the hidden attribute and open the list before it was asked for.
